(a) we can use Bayesian priors to derive optimal stopping policies for adaptive algorithms, and (b) these policies offer significant improvement over existing methods for selecting the best hyperparameters for neural networks.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the Bayesian prior can be used to inform the optimal early stopping policy.

, when the cost of a single run of the algorithm is large, the optimal policy can be very different than the optimal policy when run cost is small, and that the optimal policies are often very different from what is used in practice.

, in the context of black-box optimization, it is possible to derive an optimal early-stopping policy for any Bayesian prior over algorithm run-times, and that this policy is typically much more effective than a simple thresholding policy that stops whenever a run's accuracy is below-moderate.
